title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Life Skills: Stress, Conflict and Change

questions.prompt: What is positive, short-term stress that improves performance called?
Which conflict style aims for a win–win outcome?
Match each conflict style to its outcome.
Contrast TWO healthy and TWO unhealthy ways of coping with exam stress.
questions.memo:
Healthy (1 each): time management; exercise; sleep; talking; relaxation
Unhealthy (1 each): procrastination; substances; isolation; aggression

questions.prompt: Bottling up feelings is a healthy long-term way to deal with stress.
Give TWO effects of long-term stress on health.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): weakened immune system; high blood pressure; depression/anxiety; sleep problems; heart disease; digestive problems

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Study Skills and Exam Preparation for Matric

questions.prompt: Testing yourself without looking at notes is called…
Match each verb to its cognitive level.
Spaced practice means revising a topic several times over a period of weeks.
What is the strategy of combining words with diagrams and visuals called? (two words)
What should you do if you cannot answer a question in an exam?
questions.memo:
✓ Move on to other questions so you do not lose time (1)
✓ Return to it later; write what you know for partial marks (1)

questions.prompt: Why are preliminary examinations important for Grade 12 learners?
questions.memo:
✓ They give practice under exam conditions (1)
✓ and show weak areas to focus on before the final exams (1)

questions.prompt: Lifestyle diseases are also called non-… diseases. (one word)
Too much salt is a major risk factor for…
Which vaccine helps prevent cervical cancer?
Calculate the BMI of a person with mass 64 kg and height 1,60 m.
Family history is a risk factor that cannot be changed.
Match each disease to a major risk factor.
Suggest THREE lifestyle changes that reduce the risk of heart disease.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): stop smoking; exercise; healthy diet; less salt; maintain healthy weight; manage stress; limit alcohol

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Human Rights Violations and Responsible Citizenship

questions.prompt: What is a human rights violation?
questions.memo:
✓ When a person's rights in the Bill of Rights (1)
✓ are denied or abused by the state, organisations or individuals (1)

questions.prompt: Which right is violated when learners are taught in collapsing classrooms without textbooks?
Match each violation to a right affected.

pairs.right: Freedom and security of the person

questions.prompt: The media can help address human rights violations by exposing them.
Discuss THREE causes of human rights violations in South Africa.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): poverty and inequality; prejudice; lack of rights education; weak law enforcement; corruption; abuse of power

questions.prompt: Give TWO actions of a responsible citizen when they witness a human rights violation.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): report it to police/SAHRC; support the victim; document evidence safely; speak out; join campaigns

questions.prompt: Which Chapter 9 institution investigates maladministration and abuse of power in government? (two words)
